messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] error multi_normal
parts:
The problem is that the first argument needs to be a vector, not
a row vector. Here's the relevant part of the error message:

> TRANSLATING MODEL 'mod' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
> Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name, :
> failed to parse Stan model 'mod' with error message:
> EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=23, column=37
>
> phi[1] ~ multi_normal( mu0p , C0p );
> ^-- here
>
>
> DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
> no matches for function name="multi_normal_log"
> arg 0 type=row vector
> arg 1 type=vector
> arg 2 type=matrix
> available function signatures for multi_normal_log:
> 0. multi_normal_log(vector, vector, matrix) : real

The first part says that you called multi_normal with phi[1] a row_vector,
mu0p a vector, and c0p a matrix.

The second part says the only argument pattern support is (vector, vector, matrix).

The easy solution is to transpose phi[1]:
phi[1]' ~ multi_normal( mu0p , C0p );

A more efficient approach is to declare phi
as an array of vectors:

vector[N] phi[T];

Then you can use your original version and there's
no copying required anywhere internally. There's a manual chapter up
front discussing the differences between arrays and matrices and
their efficiencies and restrictions.

- Bob

parts:
Thanks for sharing the data.

I'm afraid I don't have any suggestions for a workaround.

We're working on our error checking tolerances, which
are also causing failures in high-dimensional correlation
matrices. These both use Cholesky factors as unconstrained
representations, but I'd have expected the covariance matrix
decomposition to be pretty stable.

The issue is arithmetic, not mathematical. That is, if
we were operating on real numbers, we wouldn't have this
problem. Big matrix operations and exponentiation (to keep
the Cholesky factor's diagonal positive) on floating point is a whole
different business.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] error multi_normal
parts:
Given that all of the covariance matrices you use are
declared as parameters, I think this is a bug on our
side with validating the positive definiteness too strictly.

To debug, I'd start by trying to figure out which instance is
causing the problem. You can comment all the multi_normal out and
then reintroduce them one by one (with all others commented
out) to isolate the issue.

One problem you might have is that only sigma and omega
have priors --- this shouldn't be an issue with init, though.

It's too bad we don't do a better job of isolating the line throwing
the error in Stan --- we only tell you the type of distribution, not which
particular instance. We have some vague plans to try to fix this
in the future, but it's a surprisingly huge amount of work
(though I'm sure eventually worth the investment if we can do
it without too much of a slowdown in most cases).

- Bob
